memo.executive_summary: 50 MW Qatar powered-shell: underwriteable at 18.2% levered IRR / 5.85x MOIC if anchor LOI + KAHRAMAA MOU + transformer LoI precede financing close

jargon_translations.IRR: the annual % return on the money invested, accounting for timing
jargon_translations.PUE: how much extra power the building uses for cooling — 1.4 means 40% on top of the computing power
jargon_translations.DSCR: how comfortably rental income covers the loan payments — higher is safer
jargon_translations.payback: how many years until the cash returned equals the cash invested

simplified_takeaways: This is a real-estate-style deal: we build the building and power, the tenant brings their own AI chips and signs a long lease. Returns come from rent, not from running computers.
The numbers look strong (money roughly 5.8x over 7 years) but one coverage figure in the model is too good to be true — we must rebuild it before committing capital.
The biggest risk is not building — it's electricity. Big transformers take ~22 months and the grid hookup takes ~24 months, so we must order power gear and file the grid request on day one.
Qatar gives us a tax-free zone, the cheapest power in the region, and fast permits — but only works profitably if a big tenant signs before we break ground.
Best funding route is the QIA-Brookfield partnership, which is actively looking for exactly this kind of asset.
explainability.why_this_recommendation: We recommend a 50 MW Tier III powered-shell, anchor-leased before ground-break and financed through the QIA-Brookfield vehicle, because Qatar's power-and-permit scarcity supports a defensible $120/kW/mo rent and an 18.2% return, supported by [brookfield_qia_partnership_unlock] and [wholesale_rent_growth_momentum]. The deal makes money as a landlord, not a chip operator — which is why we avoid GPU ownership and its utilization risk. The single condition that makes or breaks the timeline is ordering transformers and filing the grid connection on day one; the single condition that makes or breaks the returns is signing an anchor tenant for at least 60% of capacity before construction starts. Before final commitment, the coverage ratio in the model must be re-derived, because as reported it is not consistent with the loan size.

decision_tensions.verdict: Tilt to a balanced Tier III (N+1), not Tier IV. Choosing Tier III over Tier IV because the binding constraint is electrical lead time (22-mo transformer, 24-mo grid) not redundancy, and anchor SLAs are met at 99.982% — accepting ~13 bps higher SLA-credit exposure and 4-8 months faster COD. Tier IV's 30-36mo COD compounds the already-fixed grid timeline without commercial payoff in an emerging market.

Tilt to aggressive pre-COD commercialization, Khazna-style with sovereign backstop. Choosing to sign anchor LOI covering >=60% before ground-break over conservative phased absorption because GCC oversupply probability is 25% without an anchor (gcc_oversupply_risk_2027) and speculative build risks 400-600 bps IRR compression — accepting >70% sovereign tenant concentration as the specific cost, mitigated by a pre-agreed sale-leaseback exit.

strategic_context.body: Qatar is an emerging DC market (absorption ~80 MW/yr, 600 MW realistic pipeline to 2030) where supply is gated by power and permits, not demand — keeping 2027 oversupply risk low and the +10-15% scarcity premium intact. The structural unlock is the QIA-Brookfield $20B AI partnership (May 2024), which makes a QFZA-domiciled, anchor-backed powered shell financeable at 60-65% LTV without a 6-12 month general capital raise. QFZA delivers a 0% corporate tax / 100% foreign ownership / 6-month permit regime (qfza_tax_regime, mena_permit_timeline_free_zone) versus 18-24 months elsewhere. The binding constraint is electrical procurement: 22-month transformers and a 24-month KAHRAMAA connection define the timeline, not the building. For an investor, the thesis is a power-and-permit-arbitrage NNN asset with sovereign-anchored absorption — attractive returns conditional on disciplined sequencing.

reality_check_flags: Electrical procurement is the binding critical path: without transformer LoI in hand at T0, energisation slips to late 2027-2029 (transformer_shortage_global + qatar_grid_connection_timeline). Theoretically sound, but operationally unrealistic before 2028 COD if KAHRAMAA and QFZA are sequenced in series rather than parallel.
MV switchgear (15-mo) must be ordered alongside transformers or electrical energisation slips 3-6 months.

Reported DSCR of 9.10x is internally inconsistent with 60% leverage @6.5% and stabilized EBITDA reported N/A — underwriteable as a base case only once EBITDA is restored and coverage re-derived; financing close before that is not advisable.
Wet-cooling design will not clear KAHRAMAA environmental review post-2025 — closed-loop adiabatic + DLC mandatory, +$1.5M/MW; confirm this premium is inside the $440M CAPEX.

structural_differences: Equinix's $165/kW/mo is retail colo with a 470k+ cross-connect interconnect moat (full-stack operator incl. fit-out + ops) — not comparable to a Qatar powered-shell landlord; our $120 sits correctly between DLR wholesale and Equinix retail, not at Equinix level.

Digital Realty's 43% EBITDA margin is a global public-REIT blend including operations; a QFZA NNN powered-shell landlord targets 55-65% because the tenant carries fit-out and ops cost — so DLR's margin understates our structure.

CoreWeave's metrics describe a GPU owner with utilization and customer-concentration risk (Microsoft anchor) and 4.5x leverage — irrelevant to return mechanics of a shell landlord, useful only as a cautionary util/concentration benchmark.

Khazna is the closest structural comp (GCC, sovereign-anchored, ~80% occupancy) but rides DEWA/EWEC power and UAE national fabric, not KAHRAMAA monopoly tariff — so its lease-up backstop is more proven than Qatar's emerging market.

infrastructure_analysis.body: 50 MW IT load at PUE 1.4 (air-cooled floor for Qatar; no year-round free-cooling window). Water stress at 4.7/5 forces closed-loop adiabatic + DLC hybrid from day one — wet-cooling will not clear KAHRAMAA environmental review post-2025, adding ~$1.5M/MW cooling premium (qatar_water_stress_premium). Powered-shell archetype means Hearst delivers shell + MEP + substation under NNN; tenant funds fit-out and owns GPUs, so this is a landlord/real-estate return, not a GPU-cloud return. Tier III (N+1) is the commercial sweet spot vs Tier IV given anchor SLAs. KAHRAMAA grid headroom (~8 GW) exists but a new 50 MW connection is a fixed 24-month process. PUE floor improves to ~1.2 only on liquid-cooled GPU halls.
tradeoffs: Choosing Tier III (N+1) over Tier IV (N+N) because anchor hyperscale/sovereign SLAs are met at 99.982% and COD lands 4-8 months sooner, accepting ~13 bps higher annual SLA-credit exposure if uptime dips.

Choosing powered-shell NNN over neocloud GPU ownership because it removes GPU obsolescence and utilization risk (CoreWeave post-ramp 78% util, crwv_utilization_post_ramp), accepting lower revenue/MW (~$120/kW/mo vs GPU-hour upside).
Choosing closed-loop adiabatic + DLC over wet-tower cooling because wet-cooling fails KAHRAMAA review, accepting +$1.5M/MW (~$75M on 50 MW) capex.
Choosing air-cooled PUE 1.4 base over full-liquid PUE 1.2 because anchor may not be GPU-dense at COD, accepting higher opex/MWh until liquid retrofit ($750K/MW) is triggered by tenant demand.

ALTERNATIVE considered: neocloud GPU-ownership — rejected because it imports utilization risk (78% post-ramp, crwv_utilization_post_ramp) and GPU obsolescence onto a real-estate investor balance sheet. RISK accepted: Tier III (not IV) carries ~13 bps higher SLA-credit exposure and sovereign anchor >70% concentration. METRIC of success: DSCR > 1.4x sustained after Year 2 stabilization (NOT the reported 9.10x, which must be re-derived) and Phase 1 occupancy >=80% at COD.

long_term_strategic_value.ten_year_arc: Phase 1 (25-50 MW) establishes a QFZA-domiciled, sovereign-anchored NNN asset financeable through the QIA-Brookfield channel. Over a 7-year hold the asset compounds on 3% rent escalation and 12% market rent momentum into a Yr7 exit (TV ~$1180M [LOW confidence, exit cap undisclosed]) via sale-leaseback to Brookfield/Blackstone or roll-up into a regional platform. Beyond 7 years, expansion to the ~600 MW Qatar 2030 pipeline positions Hearst as a multi-asset GCC platform alongside Khazna, with Qatar's $42/MWh tariff (lowest in GCC) as the durable cost moat.

LOW VISIBILITY: liquid/immersion retrofit wave 2026-2028 enabling GPU-dense re-tenanting at higher $/MW.
LOW VISIBILITY: Qatar subsea cable convergence (Ooredoo/Vodafone) turning the asset into a regional interconnect node, adding margin beyond the colo cabinet.

commercialization_strategy.pricing: $120/kW/mo hyperscale NNN base (between DLR wholesale $95 and Equinix retail $165), defensible with Qatar +10-15% scarcity premium; build in 3% annual escalation. Power passed through to tenant at KAHRAMAA tariff (~$42-45/MWh, kahramaa_tariff_industrial).
commercialization_strategy.ramp_profile: Powered-shell single-anchor: ~80% occupancy at COD, ~90% by Year 2 (per operational benchmark). Sovereign workload ramp may lag capacity by 1-2 years — model conservative 80% Yr1 / 90% Yr2 stabilization, not retail colo curve.
commercialization_strategy.anchor_tenant: Dual-track: (1) sovereign workload via QIA channel (high backstop, >70% Phase 1), (2) hyperscaler via procurement teams running >=2 in parallel for leverage. Gate construction on signed LOI covering >=60% capacity.
commercialization_strategy.contract_structure: 15-year triple-net (NNN) lease, take-or-pay on contracted MW, anchor funds fit-out + GPUs. Target hyperscale lease term 14yr (market avg). Conditional BTS with 30-40% anchor build contribution to cap vacancy.
